entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the 3 rd accused in the above case.

Annexure -A1 is the FIR which was registered based on a complaint filed before the Jurisdictional Court, which was forwarded under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
2.

The prosecution case is that the accused Nos.1 and 2 received some money for the sale of a property near Amrutha hospital, Ernakulam, from the de-facto complainant and the same was transferred in the name of the 3rd accused and the above act of the accused person is to cheat the de-facto complainant and thereby committed offences under Sections 120B, 420 read with 34 IPC.
2024:KER:75089 Annexure-A3 is the final report.
According to the petitioner, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence is made out against the petitioner who is the 3rd accused.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
I also heard the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent.

4. According to the petitioner, there were some financial transactions between the 1st accused and the de- facto complainant and the date on which the accused number 2 transferred the property in favour of the petitioner, she entered into an agreement for sale of the same property to the de-facto complainant.
Annexure-A9 is the agreement.
It is further submitted that the de-facto complainant entered into an agreement with one Mr.Rajeevan who was allegedly conducting the hotel in the property and Annexure-A10 is the agreement.
The petitioner submitted that he has not committed any breach of contract and there is no privity of contract between the petitioner and the de-facto complainant.
The petitioner submitted that, even if there is any violation of the agreement as evident in Annexure-A9 and 2024:KER:75089 Annexure-A10, the petitioner is not responsible for the same.
According to the petitioner, the dispute is only civil in nature.

The counsel appearing for Jose Thomas vs State Of Kerala on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137681369/
2 the 2nd respondent submitted that the contentions raised by the petitioner are all matters of evidence and this Court may not interfere in the proceedings pending before the Trial Court.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This considered the contention of the petitioner and the 2nd respondent.
Annexure-A3 is the final report in this case.

As per Annexure-A3, it is stated that the 1st accused made to believe the de-facto complainant that he would transfer a property in Survey No.95/17 of Edappally North near Amrutha Hospital in which Malabar restaurant is situated.
Charge witness number 1 was made to believe that the property could be assigned for Rs.1 Crore.
Accordingly, the agreement was executed on 23.09.2013.
The charge witness Number 1 paid an amount of Rs.25 Lakhs in cash and the charge witness number 1 was ready to pay the balance amount also.
But the 1 st and 2nd accused assigned the property to the 3rd accused.
Hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
Admittedly, the petitioner is 2024:KER:75089 the purchaser of the property.
This Court peruses the final report and the materials produced along with the final report.
There is nothing to show that the petitioner hatched any conspiracy with the other accused.
From the facts, it can only be seen that the petitioner, who is the 3 rd accused purchased the property from the 1st accused.
No other allegation is there against the petitioner, except the vague statements of conspiracy.
Therefore, no offence is committed by the petitioner from the materials produced by the prosecution.
But I make it clear that, this is not applicable to the other accused and the case against the other accused will be considered in accordance with law.
But the prosecution against the petitioner can be quashed.
Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner alone in C.C.No.1442/2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court IX,
Ernakulam are quashed.
